newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says 1995 mark rise more than corrected.
newsitem.headline: Buba says 1995 mark rise more than corrected.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday in its February monthly report that the mark appreciation seen in early 1995 had now more than corrected.
"The strong appreciation from the start of 1995 has been more than corrected in the meantime," the central bank said.

The Bundesbank noted in a separate section of the report that it had gone to press when the dollar was trading at 1.68 marks. The currency was trading at about 1.6850 marks early on Wednesday and has touched highs above 1.70 marks this week.

The central bank said in the report that the real value of the mark compared to the 18 most important currencies was close to the average level seen over the last 20 years when the report went to press.
"The exchange rate grid should now be much better in line with economic fundamentals than it was before," it said.
The Bundesbank attributed the recent gains in the dollar to the strength of the U.S. economy and interest rate differentials which benefited the dollar.

"Structural burdening factors, such as the unresolved deficit problems of the U.S. current account and the non-equilibrium in savings which this reflect appear to have dropped into the background in the face of the need for consolidation in Germany and Europe," the report said.

The Bundesbank also noted the strong recent rise in sterling, adding that part of the gains appeared to have been caused by demand from investors seeking to invest in currencies which they believed would not be in the future single currency.

In addition to gains created by Britain's economic strength "some investors in the pound sterling seem increasingly to see this as an alternative to the Swiss franc for investment outside the euro area," the bank said.
It noted that the Swiss franc, which was buoyed by such investment last year, had lost considerable ground to the mark in the winter months.
